findings.slide: One cut, five very different cells / Predict: what would each cell need?
findings.problem: The SoW Predict stimulus is the healing-cut image plus a split screen of five unlabelled cell outlines. No Predict slide shows the five cells. Slide 1 shows only the Amina drawing, and the five-cell hero is on the title slide. Students are asked to 'sketch one for each of the five cells' and the teacher cold-calls about 'the round cell', but nothing on screen lets students see which cell is which. The build log admits no outlines were made.
findings.fix: Put the existing art 'healing_finger_five_cells' (the five unlabelled shapes) on the first Predict slide next to or instead of the Amina drawing. Keep it unlabelled and keep it on screen through the prediction, partner talk and cold-call slides. Update the notes so the 'round cell' cold-call points to it.

findings.problem: The SoW organiser has five columns, including 'Evidence from Sickle-Cell Phenomenon'. The slide table has only four. The build log says the organiser has a sickle-cell evidence column, which contradicts the slide. Sickle-cell evidence is squeezed into the red blood cell row later.
findings.fix: Add the fifth column 'Evidence from sickle-cell phenomenon' to the slide table, as the SoW specifies. Say in the notes that it is filled in after the sickle-cell slides. Or log the omission honestly as a deliberate change.

findings.problem: The notes say 'Project a completed organiser. Click through one cell at a time.' No such slide or reveal exists. The glance materials list does not include a completed organiser. The teacher has to build it from the answer key during the lesson.
findings.fix: Add a completed-organiser slide with one reveal per cell, or add a note that the teacher must prepare it. List it on the glance slide. Keep it hidden until groups finish their own organisers.

findings.problem: This is a student pair-argument task with an empty answer_key and student_task false. The target reasoning (shape blocks small vessels and reduces oxygen delivery) appears only in the next slide's look_for and answer key.
findings.fix: Set student_task to true. Add a short answer key: the abnormal shape stops the cell passing through small vessels and reduces oxygen delivery, even though haemoglobin is present.

findings.slide: Unit map / Goals and key words
findings.problem: The goals ('structure fits function', 'built for their jobs') and the unit map title 'Cell Specialisation' show the lesson's answer before Predict. The build log claims the term is shown only on the Driving Question Board slide, which is not true.
findings.fix: Keep the unit map and goal wording as the SoW and manual require. Correct the build-log claim. Consider softer goals such as 'Investigate how five animal cells are built' so the answer is not stated.

findings.slide: Add specialised cells to your model
findings.problem: The slide, notes and look_for add a required line 'This model is based on evidence from ...'. The SoW does not ask for it and it is not logged.
findings.fix: Remove the evidence line from the student task. Or log it as an added activity and keep it optional.

findings.problem: The fallback says 'Use ARES video only as a last resort'. The red blood cell videos are marked do_not_use, and the other videos are preview_first. The fallback also uses the sickle drawing in place of missing micrograph cards, which breaks the Explain sequence.
findings.fix: Remove the ARES video fallback. Give a fallback that does not spoil: for example, the teacher projects or sketches the micrograph descriptions, and the sickle drawing is shown only in Explain.

findings.problem: The SoW has a 1-minute warning at 14 minutes and a visible 15-minute timer for the whole Observe phase. The deck uses separate 2:00 slide timers and has no 14-minute warning. The 3-minute micrograph slide is the only free-look time. The SoW lets groups look at everything at any time.
findings.fix: Add a note to give a 1-minute warning near the end of the micrograph slide. Allow early finishers to move on. Say the per-cell timers are a guide within the 15 minutes.

findings.slide: Model closing / Test our model claim
findings.problem: For the SoW owner: the SoW closing line points to tissues next lesson, but Lesson 9 is specialised plant cells. The deck omitted the SoW line and used the storyline instead (logged). Also, slide 1 says 'Five cells helped to heal this finger', which is false for the sperm cell. The SoW itself says this, and the deck handles it only in later notes.
findings.fix: No deck change beyond keeping the log entry. The SoW owner should correct the tissue teaser and the claim that all five cells help heal the cut.

build_log.sow_says: Cold-call one group per cell — say: 'Group 2, give me your CER for the red blood cell — Claim, Evidence, Reasoning.' After each response, ask the class: 'Does any group want to add or challenge?'
build_log.deck_does: Keeps the share-out exactly as the SoW describes it. An earlier draft added a step where students mark their predictions right or wrong in a different colour. That step has been removed from the slide, notes and answer key.
build_log.why: The SoW has no return-to-predictions step in this lesson. The Predict phase says 'Do not confirm or correct'. The deck must not add activities.

build_log.sow_says: Predictions are recorded on the board and in a sticky-note cluster 'What we THINK we know — Lesson 8'. The Explain phase does not say students go back to them.
build_log.deck_does: Does not add a step to revisit the predictions in Explain.
build_log.why: The manual expects students to return to their predictions in Explain. The SoW owner may want to add this step. Teachers can refer back to the predictions in the Driving Question Board discussion if they wish.

build_log.sow_says: Stated times: Predict 3 + 2 minutes; Observe 15; Explain 20 + 10 + 3; Driving Question Board 3 + 5; Model Building 10. Re-anchor, cold-call share-out, sickle-cell display and the next-lesson closing have no stated times.
build_log.deck_does: Explain organiser trimmed 20 to 16 minutes and CER share-out 10 to 8 minutes. Model Building 10 to 9 minutes. All other stated times are kept. Predict totals 9 minutes (1 re-anchor, 3, 2, 3 cold-call share). Observe totals 15. Time is given to the sickle-cell display (1) and written CER (3).
build_log.why: The unstated activities need time, so the lesson must fit 80 minutes in total with unit map, goals and summary. No activity is cut and no phase loses more than 20%.

build_log.slide: Write your CER: shape and function
build_log.sow_says: 'The teacher uses the Claim-Evidence-Reasoning (CER) frame to scaffold responses' and 'Learners argue from evidence in pairs for 3 minutes before a whole-class cold-call.'
build_log.deck_does: Shows the CER frame on the slide, cold-calls 3 students, then lets every student write a short CER in the red blood cell row of the organiser.
build_log.why: The SoW gives no time or format for individual writing, but the organiser has a sickle-cell evidence column and the manual asks Explain to end with a written explanation. Teacher checker to confirm.

build_log.sow_says: 'how does that connect to what happened the day that Form 1 student in Nairobi cut their finger?' (and the unit phenomenon: 'A Form 1 student in Nairobi')
build_log.deck_does: Says 'a student in Nairobi' in the teacher's spoken lines. The word 'Form 1' is not used on any slide.
build_log.why: Manual: use CBE terms, never 'Form 1'. The SoW phenomenon text should say Grade 10 or just 'a student'. Please update the SoW.

build_log.sow_says: Lesson plan says 'Sub-Strand 1.1: Cell Structure'. The unit text says 'Sub-Strand 1.3: Cell Structure and Specialisation' and the Model Building phase says the model was 'begun in Lesson 1' while the unit storyline says the cumulative model begins in Lesson 2.
build_log.deck_does: Uses 'Cell Structure' and Lesson 8 as given. Model Building slide simply says 'your cumulative model'.
build_log.why: The sub-strand number and the start of the cumulative model are labelled differently in different parts of the SoW. The SoW owner should choose one version.

build_log.sow_says: Purpose: 'if all cells share the same DNA, why do platelets, neutrophils, fibroblasts, and epidermal cells look so radically different?' Overview: 'All five cells are explicitly connected to their roles in the healing-cut sequence.'
build_log.deck_does: Teaches the five cells the Observe phase names (red blood, white blood, nerve, sperm, muscle). The sperm cell row says it is not directly involved in healing. Platelets, fibroblasts and epidermal cells are not studied.
build_log.why: The cells in the phenomenon do not match the five cells in the lesson, and a sperm cell has no role in healing. The SoW owner should check the storyline.

build_log.sow_says: Observe pack says 'parallel myofilaments'. The muscle cell diagram template labels 'myofibrils'.
build_log.deck_does: Shows the diagram label 'myofibrils' and the pack note 'parallel myofilaments' as written. Notes tell the teacher to use the pack word.
build_log.why: Two different terms for the same structure. The SoW owner should choose one.

build_log.sow_says: Pack: 'synaptic knobs'. The nerve cell diagram template labels 'axon terminals'.
build_log.deck_does: Shows 'axon terminals' on the diagram and 'synaptic knobs' in the pack notes. The teacher notes say they are the same thing.
build_log.why: Two different terms for the same structure.

build_log.sow_says: White blood cell: 'irregular lobed nucleus, many lysosomes, flexible membrane'.
build_log.deck_does: The white blood cell template has no lysosome label, so lysosomes appear in the pack notes line only.
build_log.why: The drawing cannot show lysosomes. The teacher reads the pack notes aloud.

build_log.sow_says: 'two printed micrograph images (one showing normal red blood cells vs. sickle cells; one showing a nerve cell stained with methylene blue)' and 'a data card'.
build_log.deck_does: Describes the micrograph cards and gives the data card text on the slide. No micrograph images are made. The teacher must supply the printed cards or project them.
build_log.why: The SoW does not give the images. Teacher checker to confirm that the cards exist.

build_log.sow_says: 'groups that can connect the 120-day lifespan to the absence of a nucleus (no energy wasted on DNA replication) are demonstrating advanced reasoning'
build_log.deck_does: Keeps this as a listening point in the notes only. It is not on a slide.
build_log.why: A red blood cell without a nucleus cannot repair itself or make new proteins, which is one reason it lives only about 120 days. The idea 'no energy wasted on DNA replication' links lifespan and nucleus in a way that may be misleading. Please check.

build_log.sow_says: Evidence pack, prediction sheet, Structure-Function Graphic Organiser, enlarged cell diagrams, sticky notes.
build_log.deck_does: Writes only these items. No quantities per group are given.
build_log.why: The SoW gives no quantities or details of materials. The glance slide cannot list them.

build_log.sow_says: Listen for the key reasoning: the abnormal shape prevents the cell from passing through small blood vessels and reduces its ability to carry oxygen efficiently.
build_log.deck_does: Answer keys and teacher prompts use the idea of a 'narrow gate' in the if_then. The sickle cell is described as 'long and curved like a crescent'.
build_log.why: The crescent description is a standard textbook fact, not stated in the SoW. Teacher to verify against the micrograph card.

build_log.sow_says: Nerve cell: 'long axon, myelin sheath, dendrites, synaptic knobs'. Muscle cell: 'many mitochondria, parallel myofilaments, multinucleate'.
build_log.deck_does: Answer keys say the myelin sheath helps the signal move quickly, and that mitochondria release energy and myofilaments make the cell shorten. Also: mature human red blood cells have lost their nucleus (science note on Observe: Red blood cell).
build_log.why: These are established textbook facts the SoW does not state. Teacher to verify.

build_log.sow_says: 'the teacher displays the micrograph comparison (normal vs. sickle RBCs)'
build_log.deck_does: Uses a new drawing, 'sickle_vs_normal_red_cells', labelled as a drawing, as the display in Explain. The photo micrograph card is the printed card from Observe.
build_log.why: Only drawn illustrations are allowed in decks. The drawing is a new scene. Teacher checker to check it shows sickle cells correctly.

build_log.sow_says: No ARES resources are named in the SoW.
build_log.deck_does: Attaches explain.video (Anatomy of a neuron) and explain.reading (Nerve Cells, CK-12) to the share-out slide only. Both are marked 'Preview first' in the notes.
build_log.why: They fit the nerve cell only and are not an exact match. The two resources about red blood cells are not placed on student slides.

build_log.sow_says: No hazardous materials are used in this lesson. If printed micrograph cards are handled, ensure hands are washed before and after.
build_log.deck_does: is_practical is false and there is no Safety slide. The handwashing line and the sensitivity advice for sickle-cell are in the Observe notes, the sickle-cell slide notes and the title-slide purpose and before-class lists.
build_log.why: Students work only with diagrams, cards and writing. Teacher checker to confirm that no Safety slide is needed.

build_log.sow_says: Model Building: 'Next lesson, we go deeper — we will ask: if individual cells are specialised, what happens when many of the same specialised cell work together? That is the question of tissues'. The storyline says Lesson 9 is 'Specialised Plant Cells' and tissues come in Lesson 10.
build_log.deck_does: The next-lesson teaser follows the storyline: specialised plant cells. The tissues sentence is not used in the deck.
build_log.why: The closing line in the SoW does not match the next lesson's title. SoW owner to correct one of them.

build_log.sow_says: Purpose: 'To enable learners to explain the concept of cell specialisation'. Lesson 8 is titled 'Cell Specialisation'.
build_log.deck_does: Goals and key words avoid the term 'cell specialisation'. The term is shown only on the Driving Question Board slide, after the class vote.
build_log.why: Goals and key words are shown before Predict. Naming the idea early would give away the explanation. The lesson title still contains the term. Teacher checker to confirm this is acceptable.

build_log.slide: One cut, five very different cells
build_log.sow_says: 'Display the phenomenon image and the five cell outlines side by side.' Learners are 'shown the phenomenon anchor image (a close-up of a healing finger cut) and a split-screen showing five unlabelled micrograph outlines'.
build_log.deck_does: The title-slide hero shows a magnifying glass over a plastered fingertip with five cells. The healing-finger drawing is on the first Predict slide. No separate outline images were made.
build_log.why: The SoW does not supply the close-up image or the five outlines. Teacher to supply them or use the hero drawing.

build_log.sow_says: Teacher reflection: 'consider using a second supporting phenomenon at the start of Lesson 9 (e.g., the effect of dehydration on red blood cell shape in long-distance runners like Eliud Kipchoge's training regime)'.
build_log.deck_does: Not used on any slide or in the notes. The reflection questions only ask whether to plan another example.
build_log.why: This example is not part of today's activities. The claim about dehydration and red blood cell shape is not supported in the SoW. SoW owner to check it.

build_log.sow_says: No ARES resources are named in the SoW.
build_log.deck_does: Red blood cell videos (predict.video, observe.video) are marked do_not_use because they would explain the cell too early. Nerve cell and muscle cell resources are preview_first. Only explain.video and explain.reading are placed on a slide.
build_log.why: No resource gives an exact match for all five cells. None is needed to run the lesson.
